subject: BIOLOGY
pageTitle: Punnett Squares: Genotype and Phenotype Ratios Explained
description: Fill in a Punnett square, read genotype and phenotype ratios, and avoid the mistake of thinking offspring must match the ratio exactly.
caption: Punnett squares in 7 swipes: genotype vs phenotype, how to fill the grid, and two worked examples. Free Biology study guide at precisstudy.com/biology (no sign-up).

slides.title: THE VOCABULARY
slides.note: Genotype is the code. Phenotype is what you see.

slides.title: HOW TO FILL IT IN
lines: Put one parent's alleles across the top
Put the other parent's down the side
Combine each row with each column
slides.note: Each of the four boxes is an equally likely offspring.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: Tt × Tt. What fraction is tt?
steps: The four boxes are TT, Tt, Tt and tt
One box out of four is tt

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: Bb × bb. What is the genotype ratio?
steps: The four boxes are Bb, Bb, bb and bb

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Four kids from Tt × Tt must include exactly one tt
points: Each child has a 1 in 4 chance, independent of the others.
The ratio is a probability, not a guarantee.
